track_b.designed_hypothesis: Give model FAMILIES votes rather than checkpoints, so two correlated e5-large runs do not outvote an independent model (BGE).
track_b.why_it_cannot_run: out_bge and out_q15 do not exist — ameya confirms neither is on the integration machine, and the spot box that would have produced BGE's logits was destroyed at 21:40 (RESEARCH_v6 6.9). With only out_e5l and out_e5l2 there is no independent family: they correlate +0.9757 on the test band (measured here). out_e5b was not delivered and is far weaker on France (rule AUC 0.687) anyway.
track_b.alignment_proof: fam_blend.py reproduces out_cem2 from out_e5l + out_e5l2 BIT-IDENTICALLY (max|diff| 0.000e+00 on both splits), with fitted moments matching out_cem2/config.json exactly. Production standardises on all 1,568,554 train band rows, not training folds only.
track_b.screener_validated: French rule AUC measured here vs published: out_e5l 0.8026 vs 0.803, out_e5l2 0.7919 vs 0.792, out_cem2 0.8062 vs 0.806. Exact agreement on 53,290 band pairs at 57.6% true-copy share.
track_b.fallback_question: Is the equal mean the best e5l/e5l2 weighting for France? RESEARCH_v6 6.5 left this open: a 0.3/0.7 blend had a better holdout band AUC but its French behaviour was never measured.

best_vs_production.bootstrap: cluster over 47,985 S1, 1,000 resamples, 100% favour the challenger

track_b.recommendation: Do not spend a stage-2 fit or an upload slot. Statistically real, practically negligible: ~1/4 of the e5l->equal-mean step, so of order +0.0001 public, below the ~+0.00015 that separates us from rank 3. The 0.7/0.3 optimum was also selected as the argmax of a sweep scored on the same proxy it is credited on, so the CI does not correct for that selection, and the effect would still have to survive stage 2, self-training, stage 3, the rules and the acronym join.
track_b.what_would_reopen_it: out_bge, or a usable out_q15. An independent family is the whole premise.

frs2_withdrawn.my_claim: I recommended frs2 (stage-2 decision for France, skipping stage 3) as the best-motivated cheap lever, ahead of a threshold probe, estimating +0.0001 to +0.0002 LB.
frs2_withdrawn.correction: WRONG, and frs2 is withdrawn. 35% of its French drops are empty-address records that stage 3's part B lifts, and France has the same empty-address share as US/India, so there is no French-specific defect there. The stage-2-to-stage-3 rule-AUC drop I cited from 6.12 was CIRCULARITY, not evidence that stage 3 harms France.
frs2_withdrawn.independent_confirmation: fhs.py's true-copy population puts v7nst-frs2 at -3.86 net true copies per 1000 French S1 against v7nst — the worst of every candidate measured.
frs2_withdrawn.action: Do not build an frs2 package. My ordering advice that put frs2 first is retracted.

bge_lb_estimate_too_high.my_claim: Adding bge to the cross-encoder mean is worth about +0.00026 LB, from CE AUC +0.020 via stage-2 pc and implied France.
bge_lb_estimate_too_high.correction: Probably HIGH. Every hop in that calibration was measured BEFORE stage-2 self-training, and self-training absorbs most of the cross-encoder difference. Evidence: v7mst's +0.020 CE gain moves only 8 French final predictions per 1000 S1 against v7nst (+2.7 / -5.3), where v7n -> v7nst moved 31. Its US/India part is +0.000013.
bge_lb_estimate_too_high.implication: The cross-encoder mix matters less than either my CE-level number or 6.13's suggests once stage 2 is self-trained. Track B's practical ceiling is lower than +0.00026.

v7s_warning_already_covered.my_claim: v7s drops e5l2, which I measured as costing -0.00144 labelled holdout band AUC; it should be gated before being preferred.
v7s_warning_already_covered.response: The concern is accepted and the correction to 6.13 is acknowledged, but it was already covered: every variant is gated on the labelled holdout macro F0.5 by paired bootstrap (c2 and s3) before packaging, and its US/India part is compared against v7nst's 0.843210. rulepop_decision_check.what: Scores a package's FINAL matched pairs against France's rule populations (A/APP/ACR treated as true, op-B as false), rather than scoring a model's logits or pc. Built to test whether the label-free French check can rank candidate PACKAGES before an upload slot is spent.
rulepop_decision_check.headline: IT CANNOT, within the v7 family. The check is saturated at the decision level.

results.look_alike_op_B_predicted: 0 of 64,016 in every one of v6all, v7n, v7nst, v7ens2 — post_ops fully suppresses op-B, so precision on the populations is 1.0000 for all of them and carries no information
results.v7nst_vs_v7ens2: 29 disagreements out of 128,856 population pairs, ALL of them true-copy: 15 kept only by v7nst, 14 only by v7ens2. Noise.
results.v7nst_vs_v6all: 235 disagreements, 210 kept only by v7nst vs 25 only by v6all — so the check DOES resolve a large step

rulepop_decision_check.conclusion: The diagnostic has resolution for big changes (v6all -> v7n) and none within the v7 family. The label-free French check ranks CROSS-ENCODERS, where the spread is real (0.774 to 0.831), not final PACKAGES, where the rules force the populations flat. Choosing between v7nst / v7ens2 / v7s / v7sq finals cannot be done this way; only the leaderboard discriminates them.
rulepop_decision_check.caveat: post_ops deliberately forces decisions on these populations, so absolute numbers measure the rules as much as the model. Only between-package differences are model-driven. And none of it is French ground truth.
